about: Curated words for ROADMAP.md: one entry per PLAN.md milestone. Ids and statuses come from PLAN.md, releases from CHANGELOG.md headings. Edit this file, then run npm run roadmap:generate. See CONTRIBUTING.md.

entries.title: Chat panel and shortcuts
entries.summary: A Muse chat panel in the sidebar or in an editor tab, with keyboard shortcuts and settings that take effect in open panels right away.

entries.title: Sign in and chat through Muse Code
entries.summary: Sign in through your browser and chat with Muse Spark through the Muse Code CLI, with streamed replies, a Stop button and recovery when the CLI exits.

entries.title: Composer and command palette
entries.summary: The prompt box gets a / command palette, file and image attachments, @ file mentions, a model picker, effort and thinking controls, permission modes, and messages you can queue while a reply runs.

entries.title: Rich transcript
entries.summary: Replies show as Markdown with highlighted code you can copy or insert, tool calls show as rows with diffs and shell output, and approvals, questions and the task list appear inline in the chat.

entries.title: Editor context and diagnostics
entries.summary: Your open file or selection goes along with your message, unsaved editors are saved before each turn, code blocks can be applied to the editor, and the agent can read the Problems panel's errors and warnings.

entries.title: Conversation history
entries.summary: A searchable History dialog resumes and archives past conversations, offers rename and fork where the Muse Code CLI supports them, and marks hidden panels with unread replies.

entries.title: Bring your own Model API key
entries.summary: With your own Meta Model API key, the panel talks to Meta's API directly and runs its own file and shell tools inside the workspace, under the same permission modes and approval cards.

entries.title: Account and usage
entries.summary: An Account & usage dialog shows your Muse Code subscription's usage bars with reset times and this conversation's tokens, plus getting-started tips and screen-reader announcements.

entries.title: Voice dictation
entries.summary: Dictate into the prompt box with a microphone button (tap or hold, or Ctrl+D) on Windows and macOS, using the operating system's own speech recogniser at no cost.

entries.title: Workspace rules, skills and memory
entries.summary: In a trusted workspace the agent follows your AGENTS.md rules and project skills on both backends, and on the Model API backend it also gets the project memory index.

entries.title: Saved conversations and diagnostics
entries.summary: Model API conversations survive a window reload, a crash screen offers Reload instead of a blank panel, and Show Logs and Diagnostics commands help with support.

entries.title: Walkthrough and editor commands
entries.summary: A Get started walkthrough, New Conversation, Sign Out, Open in Terminal and Create AGENTS.md commands, editor-tab conversations that come back after a reload, and settings a repository cannot override.

entries.title: Fork and rewind menu
entries.summary: A menu on each of your messages forks the conversation from that point, rewinds the code edits made after it, or does both.

entries.title: Subagents and the Agent map
entries.summary: Muse Code's subagents appear in the chat with an Agent map of their transcripts and tokens, alongside choices offered as pickers and a one-click compact button.

entries.title: Scrolling, copy and output tabs
entries.summary: The chat follows new output with a jump-to-newest button, rows expand with chevrons, replies get a Copy button, and tool outputs and long diffs open in editor tabs.

entries.title: File links and live thinking
entries.summary: Tool rows link to the changed lines, stored diffs open with Click to expand, thinking streams as it happens, and question cards get tabs and an Other answer.

entries.title: Reply to and quote chat text
entries.summary: Reply to a specific output, or highlight any text in the chat and ask about it or comment on it, and the quoted context goes along with your message.

entries.title: Agent map controls
entries.summary: Each subagent keeps its own transcript in the Agent map, which can interrupt, stop, resume or close an agent, send it a note, or give it a follow-up task.

entries.title: Auto-growing prompt box
entries.summary: The prompt box grows with wrapped lines as well as new lines, up to ten rows, and then scrolls.

entries.title: Rewind across subagents
entries.summary: Rewind code to here also undoes edits made by subagents, in reverse order of when they finished.

entries.title: Workspace confinement
entries.summary: On the Model API backend, file tools refuse links that lead outside the workspace and always ask before writing sensitive config files, and git never runs in an untrusted folder.

entries.title: Reliable processes and restarts
entries.summary: A stopped or timed-out shell command ends everything it started, a stuck CLI no longer hangs the panel, and after a restart or crash the next message continues the same conversation.

entries.title: Dependable approvals and resumes
entries.summary: A resumed conversation shows its waiting approvals and questions again, an oversized message is refused with the reason, and a failed tool or stream glitch no longer breaks a Model API conversation.

entries.title: Safer file edits
entries.summary: On the Model API backend, edits keep a file's line endings, byte-order mark and encoding and never overwrite unsaved editor changes, and revert puts lines back only where the file still matches.

entries.title: Sturdier panel
entries.summary: After a crash the panel reloads with the conversation intact, and it handles input methods, right-to-left text, reduced motion and dialog focus properly.

entries.title: Platform and dictation fixes
entries.summary: Windows shortcuts no longer clash with the system, dictation explains why it is unavailable in remote windows, and the package includes third-party licence notices.

entries.title: Windows commands fully stopped
entries.summary: On Windows each shell command runs in its own job object, so Stop or a timeout ends every process it started.

entries.title: macOS dictation permissions
entries.summary: On macOS, dictation asks for microphone and speech-recognition permission under the dictation helper's own name instead of being refused without asking.

entries.title: Protected .muse folder
entries.summary: On the Model API backend, writing anything under .muse/ asks for approval in every mode except Bypass.

entries.title: Skills, imports and export
entries.summary: Turn Muse Code skills on or off, import skills from other coding agents, and export a conversation as Markdown on either backend.

entries.title: View MCP servers and hooks
entries.summary: See which MCP servers and hooks Muse Code will load, sign in to remote MCP servers, and open the files that define them, all read-only.

entries.title: Git worktrees
entries.summary: Start work on a new branch in a separate git worktree that opens in a new window, and remove worktrees with a second confirmation before uncommitted changes are discarded.

entries.title: Web search
entries.summary: On the Model API backend the agent can search the web, a paid extra that asks first, with each search shown as a paid row and its sources listed under the reply.

entries.title: Image generation
entries.summary: On the Model API backend the agent can create PNG images in your workspace, a paid extra that asks before every image with its price.

entries.title: Muse Voice dictation
entries.summary: Optional paid dictation with Meta's Muse Voice Transcribe on the Model API backend, while your computer's free speech recogniser stays the default.

entries.title: Smarter code rewind
entries.summary: Rewind code to here still undoes an edit after lines were added or removed above it, and refuses instead of guessing when the edited lines changed or appear more than once.

entries.title: Accessibility checks on every screen
entries.summary: Every screen of the panel is checked against WCAG 2.2 AA in VS Code's four default themes, and the contrast and keyboard problems those checks found are fixed.

entries.title: Slash commands as you type
entries.summary: Typing / in the prompt shows the palette, and one more letter switches to a list of slash commands and skills that narrows as you type.

entries.title: Clearer logs, smoother streaming
entries.summary: The extension's log records every failure and each turn's result and timing but never your prompts, files or model output, and streamed replies reach the panel more efficiently.

entries.title: The panel in fourteen languages
entries.summary: The panel, its commands and its settings follow the editor's display language in fourteen machine-translated languages, with English as the fallback.

entries.title: More reliable Model API conversations
entries.summary: Model API conversations in which the model writes text before a tool call no longer fail, and a reply the server cuts off is sent again automatically.

entries.title: Readable rows for every tool
entries.summary: Every tool Muse Code runs gets a named, readable row in the conversation, including memory notes, goals, schedules, web search results and pictures the agent read or made.

entries.note: program heading; its milestones have their own entries

entries.title: Image edits on both backends
entries.summary: The agent can edit or combine workspace images, and image tools and Muse Voice also work on the Muse Code backend when a Model API key is stored, billed to that key with the price confirmed first.

entries.title: Session goals
entries.summary: Set a goal with /goal that the agent keeps working toward, shown in a progress strip with Pause, Resume, Edit and Clear, on both backends.

entries.title: Your own shell, background work and answers
entries.summary: Run your own shell commands by starting a message with !, move a running command to the background and stop it, and answer the agent's questions in your own words.

entries.title: Workflow progress cards
entries.summary: Multi-agent workflows that Muse Code runs appear as live, read-only cards with each agent's state, time, tokens and result, without Cancel, Skip or Retry controls yet.

entries.title: Subagents on the Model API
entries.summary: On the Model API backend the agent can start parallel child tasks, a paid extra that asks before each new task, with the children visible and steerable in the Agent map.

entries.title: See and edit memory
entries.summary: Browse, open, create, edit and delete Muse Code's memory notes from the panel, and the Model API backend reads and writes the same notes.

entries.title: MCP servers on the Model API
entries.summary: The Model API backend runs the local and remote MCP servers from Muse Code's settings, with approvals by permission mode and a view of each server's status.

entries.title: Hooks on the Model API
entries.summary: With an opt-in setting, the Model API backend runs Muse Code's hook commands in trusted workspaces, so a hook can block or ask about a tool call.

entries.title: Scheduled prompts
entries.summary: Save a prompt on an interval or cron schedule with /loop on the Model API backend, where a due prompt runs only when you choose Run now and confirm its price.

entries.title: Conversation rewind and side chat
entries.summary: Rewind a conversation to an earlier message and branch from it, or open a Plan-mode side chat in its own panel, except with Muse Code on Windows.

entries.note: accuracy fix inside M53 (usage reset times)

entries.title: PDFs and text files as input
entries.summary: Attach PDFs on the Model API backend and UTF-8 text files from the workspace on both backends, and the agent can read workspace PDFs and images.

entries.title: Install and sign in from the panel
entries.summary: Install the Muse Code CLI and sign in with your Meta account from the panel, with the install command shown and confirmed before it runs in a terminal you can watch.

entries.title: Corporate networks and proxies
entries.summary: Proxy and HTTPS-inspection settings carry through to every request, Diagnostics shows the network setup, and a request that cannot reach Meta says why.

entries.title: Ask before every paid use
entries.summary: Every paid use asks first in a popup with Allow once, Allow always in this workspace, or Deny, in every permission mode, and Account & usage can take back an Allow always.

entries.note: host API inventory gate; no user-visible change

entries.title: Native plugins for more editors
entries.summary: Native plugins that embed the full panel in JetBrains IDEs and Visual Studio, then Eclipse, NetBeans and Jupyter, and support where each host allows it for browser-based and other editors.

entries.note: shared boundaries refactor for other editors; no user-visible change

entries.title: VS Code-based editors and Open VSX
entries.summary: The extension installs and runs in editors built on VS Code 1.99 or later, such as VSCodium, Cursor, Positron, Eclipse Theia and code-server, and is published on Open VSX.

entries.title: Muse Spark in ACP editors
entries.summary: A standalone agent brings chat, tool calls, approvals, modes and sessions to editors that speak the Agent Client Protocol, so far tried in Zed, Neovim, Emacs and JupyterLab.

entries.title: Code intelligence and rename
entries.summary: The agent finds definitions, references, symbols, hovers and call hierarchies through the editor's language services instead of searching text, and can rename a symbol everywhere it is used.

entries.note: program heading; its milestones have their own entries

entries.title: The agent checks its own edits
entries.summary: After the agent edits files, language-server errors and your own check commands reach its next request on the Model API backend, and Muse Code is asked to run the same checks.

entries.title: Web fetch
entries.summary: The model can read one public HTTPS page it found or you named, fetched from your machine at no charge on either backend, asking first wherever your permission mode asks.

entries.title: Review before it lands
entries.summary: /review checks uncommitted changes, a branch, a commit or anything you describe, with a security preset, and a review pane lets you accept, revert or comment on each change.

entries.title: Git and pull requests
entries.summary: Draft commit messages and pull requests from the conversation, commit and push only after you confirm (never with force), and keep other people's pull requests in their own worktree until you trust them.

entries.title: Turn checkpoints
entries.summary: Restore files, the conversation or both to an earlier message and redo it, with every file the restore had to leave named.

entries.title: Observation packing
entries.summary: An optional Model API setting, off by default, swaps large old tool outputs for a short placeholder the model can page back, so long sessions resend fewer tokens.

entries.title: Handoff to a new conversation
entries.summary: /handoff has the model write a brief of the goal, decisions, files and open work, which you review and edit before it starts a fresh Model API conversation.

entries.note: paired efficiency evaluation; developer tooling, nothing in the package

entries.title: Custom agents
entries.summary: Define specialised agents in AGENT.md files, each with its own prompt, tool allowlist, model, effort and permission mode, which run as paid child tasks on the Model API backend.

entries.title: Session board and best-of-N
entries.summary: A session board lists open and saved conversations with their state, branch, changed files and waiting approvals, and paid best-of-N runs one prompt in several worktrees so you can apply the best result.

entries.title: Safer Auto mode
entries.summary: Auto on the Model API backend follows standing command rules and permission profiles, and an optional paid reviewer never overrides a deny, an ask rule or a protected write.

entries.title: Plans as files
entries.summary: Save a Plan-mode reply as a Markdown file in .agents/plans/ and implement it in a fresh conversation, or reopen saved plans later from the palette.

entries.title: Headless runs and a GitHub Action
entries.summary: Run one agent turn without an editor through the ACP agent's exec command, or let a GitHub Action review or propose a fix for a same-repository pull request, both under a hard dollar budget.

entries.title: Browser check
entries.summary: After a web change the model can open your local dev server in an isolated headless browser, click and type through a few steps, and read console errors and failed requests.

entries.title: Awareness and budgets
entries.summary: A notification tells you when a long turn ends or waits while the window is unfocused, replies can show their token and dollar estimate, and a per-conversation budget caps Model API spend.

entries.title: Import from other agents
entries.summary: Bring commands, agents, project rules, MCP servers and hooks over from other coding agents, and review each one before it is saved.

entries.title: Session export, import and share
entries.summary: Export a conversation as a scrubbed portable file, open it read-only as a share file, or resume it as a new Model API conversation, with nothing uploaded.

entries.title: Restore by the model's own writes
entries.summary: Turn checkpoints are on by default and restore only the model's own file-tool writes, naming any changes made by commands, hooks or other tools that a restore does not undo.

entries.title: Panel polish
entries.summary: The chat panel gains a context ring, steps folded under one summary row, message times on hover, editable queued messages, a diff tally with Review and a collapsible tasks pane.

entries.note: program heading; its milestones have their own entries

entries.title: Bookmarks and timed sends
entries.summary: Bookmark conversations you come back to and schedule a prompt or a continue message for a time you choose.

entries.title: Bundled skills
entries.summary: Project setup, feature delivery and quality retrofit workflows ship with the extension on the Model API backend and install into Muse Code with one click.

entries.title: Auto reviewer on Muse Code
entries.summary: In Auto on the Muse Code backend, a short review turn on your Muse subscription can approve an eligible request once, and anything it doubts or cannot review still asks you.

entries.title: Hooks from other agents
entries.summary: Import hooks written for other popular coding agents and run them at the matching points, opt in and only in trusted workspaces, with unsupported events refused and the reason shown.

entries.title: Amp and OpenCode plugins
entries.summary: Amp and OpenCode plugins run as bounded hooks on the Model API backend, while the ACP agent refuses plugins and macOS refuses OpenCode plugins.

entries.title: Muse Gadgets support
entries.summary: A bundled skill guides ESP32 build, flash and bounded monitor runs on the Model API backend, Muse Gadgets tokens are redacted, and prompts holding a detected secret pause for your decision.

entries.title: Report a problem
entries.summary: Build a scrubbed problem report locally, even after a crash and without signing in, review each item, then copy it, save it or open an issue yourself, with nothing sent by the extension.

entries.title: Tab completions
entries.summary: Ghost-text code completions in the languages you enable, billed to your Model API key after a one-time price prompt and stopped by a separate hard daily budget.

entries.title: Next edit suggestions
entries.summary: Suggestions for edits away from the cursor, once the editor API they need is stable.

entries.title: Bring your own models
entries.summary: Add keys for OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, OpenRouter and other providers, or local model servers, with each key bound to the address it was entered for and features matched to each model's capabilities.

entries.title: ChatGPT and Copilot sign-in
entries.summary: Eligible ChatGPT Plus or Pro accounts sign in through the browser and compatible editors can use Copilot models, with the plan's own limits applying instead of a dollar cap.

entries.title: More providers and integrations
entries.summary: More providers such as Amazon Bedrock, chosen models offered to the editor's own chat under a daily cap, providers' own paid search, and Tab completions on other providers.

entries.title: Agent roles and teams
entries.summary: Agent roles with charters, tools, model pools and task limits, and teams of workers in isolated workspaces whose work is reviewed before it merges.

entries.title: Teams in other editors and headless runs
entries.summary: The same teams, roles, pools and caps in the ACP agent for other editors and in headless runs, each asking for approval in its own way.

entries.title: Team scheduler and traffic
entries.summary: A board of dependent tasks and a scheduler that keep every agent lane busy across worktrees and branches while avoiding collisions between them.

entries.title: Machine-wide agent coordination
entries.summary: Several windows, editors and the ACP agent sharing one machine-wide limit on workers and heavy commands.

entries.title: Legal and licence scan
entries.summary: Run /legal to scan licences, copyright headers and source provenance without a model call, export the report and apply only the header fixes you confirm, without any claim that a project is legally compliant.

entries.title: Muse Judge risk cautions
entries.summary: When you approve an action, the conversation's own model can add an advisory, uncalibrated caution about its risk but can never grant permission, while separate judge engines and calibration come in a later phase.

entries.title: What's New after updates
entries.summary: After an update, a What's New tab opens once while you are idle with each release's highlights and Try it buttons, and a fixes-only update shows a quiet notification instead.

entries.title: Paired devices
entries.summary: Link your own devices on the local network so they can take independent agent lanes and checks and hand back reviewable Git branches, without moving credentials.

entries.title: Long-task context upgrades
entries.summary: Prompts stay cache-stable, the model can search and recall packed tool output exactly, and manual compaction works in ACP editors, while automatic compaction stays off until its evaluation passes.

entries.title: Usage and cost page
entries.summary: A local Usage & Cost page shows each model call's cost, tokens, time, limits and budgets by provider, model and client, with charts, tables and exports, and the history never leaves your machine.

entries.title: Tools for makers
entries.summary: Skills, board detection, simulators and offline tools for makers, with device and machine access that never moves, heats, powers or flashes anything until you approve exactly what is sent.

entries.title: Every feature in every editor
entries.summary: Every feature working in every supported editor, through that editor's own APIs or the project's own panel, with each new feature arriving in all of them together.

entries.title: Video, audio and screen recordings
entries.summary: Attach videos, audio files, documents and screen recordings with the cost shown before sending, although sending video and audio to a model is not available yet.

entries.title: Stronger agent-loop guarantees
entries.summary: On the Model API the agent loop uses strict tool contracts, validated side answers, live tool-argument previews and concurrent read-only calls wherever the selected model supports them.

entries.title: Resource limits for your machine
entries.summary: Set CPU, memory and disk limits so background work the extension starts is slowed and then paused before the machine becomes unresponsive, while moving that work to another device is not available yet.

entries.title: Several accounts per provider
entries.summary: Keep several labelled accounts with one provider, each with its own use thresholds, see which one is in use and pin a headless run to one, so a vendor limit blocks only the affected account.

entries.title: Credential vault for agents
entries.summary: One encrypted vault for API keys, tokens, SSH keys, passwords and website logins, protected by hardware where available, from which agents get approved, logged uses of a secret but never its value.

entries.title: Muse Node
entries.summary: A headless node on a home PC, container, virtual machine, rented server or Raspberry Pi that works as a worker or orchestrator, reached from a browser, phone, terminal or editor over end-to-end encrypted links.

entries.title: Muse Desktop
entries.summary: Boot a machine from a flash drive into a Muse desktop with an installer, a workbench with chat, tabbed editors and live previews, and updates that roll back on their own if they break.

entries.title: Questions that never block
entries.summary: An agent's question stays in the dock and the transcript, the agent carries on with independent work if you have not answered after a set time, and your later answer reaches it exactly once.

entries.title: Deterministic reports
entries.summary: Run /report for project, quality, milestone, release and change reports built from local facts in Markdown, HTML, JSON or text, with saved history and comparisons, and nothing sent to a model.

entries.title: Refreshed design
entries.summary: Panel surfaces share one set of theme-aware design tokens, with consistent hover, focus and pressed states and motion that stops when reduced motion is on.

entries.title: Scheduled prompts v2
entries.summary: Schedule prompts to run once, repeatedly or on a cron expression, each with its own delivery mode, and run them unattended under a hard budget cap, so far from the terminal and ACP editors.

entries.title: Orchestrator playbook
entries.summary: The orchestration rules ship as a built-in skill that governs the panel's subagent, delegate, best-of-N and review dispatches, and /playbook shows status, records and settings locally.

entries.title: Capacity estimator
entries.summary: Run /estimate on a goal to see when it can land with your current, minimum or optimum set of agents and machines without a model call, although real forecasts are not available yet.

entries.title: Prompt library and chat sharing
entries.summary: Save prompts to a personal or project library and reuse them across workspaces, and share prompts or conversations as Markdown, HTML or JSON after an exact preview with secrets and private paths scrubbed.

entries.title: Agent outcomes and receipts
entries.summary: See each agent's activity and evidence-backed outcome, with redacted receipts and attempt history, and continue or retry it after you confirm.

entries.title: Preferred agents and handoff
entries.summary: Preferred agents for each role, with work going to the next one when the preferred agent is unavailable, the reason shown, and tasks that move to another agent partway through without losing work.

entries.title: Exact money everywhere
entries.summary: Every cost, budget and usage total kept as an exact decimal dollar amount, so the figures you see match what the budget checks enforce.

entries.note: this roadmap's generator and gate (project documentation tooling)

entries.title: Enhancements on by default
entries.summary: Model API extras are available out of the box, ask for consent before any charge and share one daily paid budget, and any setting you switched off stays off.

entries.title: Shell credential fence
entries.summary: Credential-like environment variables are kept out of the shell commands, checks, schedules, workers, hooks and Git the agent runs, and only the variables you name in a machine setting reach interactive commands.

entries.title: Help & Reference
entries.summary: /help opens a searchable page covering every feature, command, setting, slash command, CLI option and keyboard action in all fourteen translated languages, and ACP editors and the terminal get the same reference.

entries.title: Pinned question card
entries.summary: An open question or form from the agent stays as one card pinned above the chat box, and its marker in the transcript reopens and focuses it.

entries.title: Safer Windows paths
entries.summary: On Windows, ambiguous path spellings such as device paths, alternate streams, trailing dots and reserved names are refused or need a one-time manual approval, while workspaces on any drive keep working.
